title: Computing Input Length in Binary
statement: There exist a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, on every Boolean word $x$, $M$ halts within $c(|x|+1)$ steps and outputs the little-endian binary representation of the length of $x$.
hypotheses_covered: Existence of a finite Turing machine over Booleans
Existence of a natural-number constant c
Computes the binary representation of |x| within c(|x|+1) steps on every input
replaced:
There exist a finite Turing machine $M$ and a constant $c$ such that $M$
computes the function sending each input $x$ to the little-endian binary
representation of $\abs{x}$, within $c\,(n+1)$ steps on inputs of length $n$.
